title: Symmetric Encryption and Decryption Flow
description: Interactive Mermaid workflow of symmetric encryption: plaintext is encrypted to ciphertext and back, with one shared secret key feeding both the encryption and decryption steps. Includes a Kerckhoffs's-principle callout.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

learningObjectives: Explain how plaintext becomes ciphertext and back using an algorithm plus a key.
Recognize that symmetric encryption uses the same secret key in both directions.
State Kerckhoffs's principle: the algorithm is public, the key is secret.
educational.prerequisites: None beyond the intuition that a message can be scrambled and unscrambled.

pedagogical.assessment: Discussion questions ask students why the same key must appear on both sides and what Kerckhoffs's principle implies.
misconceptionsAddressed: Believing security comes from keeping the algorithm secret rather than the key.
Assuming encryption and decryption use different keys in symmetric crypto.
